draft.text: You came in because you have been feeling numbness and tingling in your right hand, especially in your thumb, index finger, and middle finger.
These symptoms have been getting worse over the last month, especially when you are typing.
You also feel pain and have trouble with fine motor tasks and grip strength in your right hand.
We found that you are 32 years old and female.
There is no history of trauma, prior treatments, or systemic conditions affecting your right hand or arm.
You mentioned that nerve conduction studies or EMG testing for your right hand were ordered, but the results are still pending.
You have not had any physical examination or imaging studies to evaluate your cervical spine or upper extremities.
You are experiencing constant numbness and tingling in your right hand, which is worse when typing.
You also have decreased grip strength and difficulty with fine motor tasks.
There are no objective findings or investigation results available to support or refute your symptoms at this time.
There is no specific plan mentioned at this time.
The next steps will be discussed once more information is available, such as the results of the nerve conduction studies or EMG testing.
